newsitem.title: CANADA: Asia Minerals sees China mine expansion.
newsitem.headline: Asia Minerals sees China mine expansion.

text.p: Asia Minerals Corp, which says it is the first foreign company to set up a gold mining joint venture in China, expects to decide by March to proceed with an expansion of the Yingezhuang gold mine.
Business manager Horst Gudemann said Thursday that a feasibility study is underway on expanding annual output at the mine to 90,000 to 100,000 ounces from 12,500 ounces.

While the first drill results will not be released until December, "we really are pretty confident (the expansion will proceed). Things look pretty good," he said in an interview at a mining conference.
The mine is in Shandong province and was previously estimated to contain 1.76 million ounces of gold. Asia Minerals has a half stake in the mine in partnership with a state-owned firm.

If the expansion does go ahead, Asia Minerals will need to raise C$32 million to finance the project. Gudemann said this would occur next summer in either one or two stages. "There definitely will be an equity offering and maybe some debt component," he said.
With the expansion, Asia Minerals hopes to cut the mine's cash production cost from US$214 an ounce to around US$160.
The company is also actively exploring in other parts of China and recently gained two new concessions. Royal Oak Mines Inc owns more than 40 percent of Asia Minerals.
